title: Choose the look of Galaxy Wristore
question: The roll assigned Station Clock for the Home screen. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Open each card's sketch to see the phone screen as written.

options.label: Station Clock
options.lineage: Hans Hilfiker's 1944 Swiss railway clock and SBB station signs
options.thesis: Your watch read like a station clock: exact, calm, and the red hand moves only when something is really happening.
options.viewport: Large title My Watch; a 60-bar minute track rings the current face, lit for how much of the watch is backed up; one blue band with the single next step; figures in tabular numerals; tab bar Watch, Faces, Apps, Discover, Backup.
options.risk: The Swiss clock is widely known; if bars and the red disc appear everywhere it becomes a theme instead of a signal.

raised.raise: Guidance blue is reserved for the next step only: one band, one message, one action per watch state.
Home shows real figures in compact rows (battery, storage, faces, apps, last backup) instead of empty hero space.
Every gauge is exact: each of the 60 bars is one sixtieth, so 38 of 55 apps backed up lights exactly 41 bars.
Model and version numbers (SM-R800, Tizen 5.5) appear once, small, never labelled twice.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: one large figure per screen, small labels, no boxes around them.

options.label: Watchmaker's Bench
options.lineage: the green bench mat, parts trays and loupe of a watch repair workshop
options.thesis: The app is the bench where your watch is serviced: every face and app laid in its tray, every picture under the loupe.
options.viewport: The watch rests on the green mat with its status on a brass-ruled tag; compartment trays below hold faces and apps; standard tab bar.
options.risk: Workshop green and brass is a familiar skeuomorphic move; if texture creeps in it reads retro instead of modern.

options.label: Watch Pass & Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: Your watch carries a pass of its vital facts, and below it a live board of everything happening to it.
options.viewport: A segmented pass for the watch (model, address, face, last backup) in tabular figures; a board of watch events and queued installs, each change held in yellow until seen; tab bar.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on showing what changed; loses on audience, since owners do not see their watch in a travel document.
options.risk: Uppercase mono labels drift toward the developer tool you ruled out.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every watch state signed like a corridor junction: one yellow band, one next step.
options.viewport: A yellow band names the next step; the watch below; arrows to each section.
options.case: Fuses poorly: owners do not picture airports when they think of their watch, and an app of signs hides the hub.
options.kept: One message per band: the next step owns a reserved colour and nothing else does.
options.risk: Reads as signage, not as an app.

options.label: High-Density Portal
options.thesis: Every fact about the watch packed onto one screen of ruled modules.
options.viewport: A mosaic of small ruled modules for faces, apps, storage and backup.
options.case: Fuses poorly: you asked for minimalistic, and density this tight turns a calm hub into a portal.
options.kept: Real figures instead of empty space.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: The watch's history as a score read upward, each event sized by its duration.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of installs, backups and restores, sized by how long each took.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract notation hides simple status.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Every face and app as a numbered catalogue entry on matte black.
options.viewport: A black field with one plot of watch activity and a small catalogue number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: names replaced by codes fail a working app; reference numbers are its one link to watch culture.
options.kept: Identifiers appear once, small, never labelled twice.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant live figure, everything else tiny labels.
options.viewport: The watch's battery figure at enormous size with a slider beneath.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type specimen has nothing to say about a watch.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Galaxy Wearable and the Apple Watch app ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A large picture of the watch, a row of face thumbnails, then grouped lists of settings.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Samsung's own app by design.
